scope: Independent read-only spec compliance followed by code-quality review and public-API synthetic localhost counterexamples. No Git mutations, production edits, original-client/application execution, account/profile/cache access, or build.

facts: Duration originates from the freshly fetched exact TrackInfo interval, not renderer options. It is read only by lease scheduling and is absent from content identity and provider actual-source metadata.
Target bytes use identity-verified tail-excluded source.length with BigInt ceiling arithmetic, 512 KiB rounding, minimum 4 and maximum 16 blocks; invalid duration remains 4 blocks.
Transport and compressed-block memory are separate global FIFO owners (8 transport, 32 memory). Both the first streaming range and future buffered ranges reserve memory before transport.

Per-response inFlight starts at 1 for the initial range and caps at 4. blocks.size plus firstPending counts retained/reserved response blocks toward the duration-derived cap, including in-flight or memory-waiting work.
Future completed EOF releases transport before resolving block.done and pumping new work, while its memory permit remains until ordered consumption or discard.
First data is written without waiting for prefill. The consumer loop and completion pump preserve order, absolute offsets and one response transform.
One unpublished-block retry retains both permits and the original retry deadline remainder. Authentication/identity/EOF/cancel behavior remains terminal or in the existing single-refresh path.

Failure/revocation aborts the controller before awaiting outstanding blocks, preventing .then callbacks from pumping more work; memory is discarded and idempotent release closures return both credit kinds.
A published lease retains one exact resolver/session transaction and fixed identity. Refresh does not create a new lease or extend its fixed expiry.

notes: No second media identity/cache owner or persistent media cache was introduced.
Memory-before-transport prevents the direct cyclic wait where every transport permit is held by a task waiting for retained-block memory.
Global FIFO first admission is preserved relative to later completion-pump jobs; a slow response can still retain its bounded memory until consumption or lease cancellation/expiry.
The concurrency budget intentionally covers participating parallel Range owners, not resolver preflight, small GETs, every socket or every network operation.
The 16 MiB limit concerns reserved/owned compressed-block credits; socket/Undici buffers, transformed response buffers and total RSS are outside that bound.

externalCases.case: Two paused initial streams and 30 completed future blocks consume all 32 memory credits; a third first stream issues no GET until one prior lease is canceled. It then receives first admission and fills its own 16-credit window. No post-revoke growth.

Three future fetches ignore cancellation and resolve late with body.cancel promises that never settle. Revocation still disposes the three late bodies, does not pump more work, and a replacement lease completes 16 MiB on the same proxy, demonstrating both credit kinds were returned.

Three future 403s share one unresolved refresh; revocation happens before its source arrives. Late source disposal reaches all six resolver owners, fetch count remains four, and the revoked lease returns 404. No grant revival or late pump.

limits: Synthetic validation does not establish a cold local-cache baseline, native QQ path selection, real CDN behavior, or absence of stutter on all songs/networks.
Original QQ's adaptive whole-file fallback is not implemented or claimed; this remains a finite 2..8 MiB read-ahead policy.
